summary.text: The Virgo Cluster is a cluster of about 1,300 galaxies, possibly up to 2,000, centered roughly 53.8 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo.
It forms the heart of the larger Virgo Supercluster, which includes the Local Group that holds the Milky Way.
Its large mass slows the Local Group's recession from the cluster, and many of its galaxies move at very high speeds.

items.prompt: You map the Virgo Cluster's galaxies by type. How do the elliptical galaxies sit compared with the spirals?

options.label: More concentrated toward the center
Spread evenly through the cluster
Gathered at the outer edges
Lined up in one long filament

items.explain: The elliptical galaxies are more centrally concentrated than the spiral galaxies.

items.prompt: A galaxy moving through Virgo stops making new stars. What in the cluster could be responsible?

options.label: The galaxy's stars have all died off
Pressure from the dense gas between galaxies strips out its gas
Dark matter absorbs its star-forming gas
Nearby galaxies steal its newest stars

items.explain: Ram pressure from the dense intracluster medium removes molecular gas, which can quench star formation.

items.prompt: The Local Group is moving away from the Virgo Cluster. How does Virgo's gravity affect that motion?

options.label: It speeds the recession up
It reverses the motion entirely
It slows the recession down
It has no effect on it

items.explain: The cluster's large mass slows the recession of the Local Group from the cluster.

items.prompt: Some stars in the Virgo Cluster float between galaxies instead of belonging to one. What is the theorized origin?

options.label: They formed in empty space between galaxies long ago
They are the leftover remains of long dead galaxies
They fell in from far outside the whole cluster
Interactions with other galaxies threw them out of home

items.explain: Intergalactic stars in the intracluster medium are theorized to have been expelled from their home galaxies by interactions with other galaxies.

items.prompt: What observation points to the Virgo Cluster having a very large mass?

options.label: Many galaxies in it move at very high speeds
Its member galaxies are all very bright
Its member galaxies sit packed in perfect rows
It contains only elliptical galaxies and no spirals

items.explain: The large mass is indicated by the high peculiar velocities of many of its galaxies.

items.prompt: Why would an X-ray telescope detect the space between Virgo's galaxies?

options.label: Dark matter glows there in X-rays
A hot, thin plasma fills it and emits X-rays
Stars there are all young and hot
Gas there collapses into black holes

items.explain: Virgo's intracluster medium is filled with a hot, rarefied plasma that emits X-rays.
